meanings: (of an aircraft or rocket) to take off
(fig.) (of an enterprise etc) to start to develop rapidly

components.note: 走 (to walk/run) — 起 relates to standing up and setting into motion.
己 (jǐ) gives a close sound cue — 起 is pronounced qǐ, sharing the same final sound.
A simplified pictograph of a bird's wings spread in flight — the source of 飞's meaning 'to fly.'

example.hanzi: 飞机马上就要起飞了。
example.pinyin: fēijī mǎshàng jiù yào qǐfēi le.
example.english: The airplane is about to take off.
example.fact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 near Kitty Hawk lasted only 12 seconds and covered about 37 meters — shorter than the wingspan of many modern airliners. Today, a Boeing 747 needs roughly 2-3 kilometers of runway to reach takeoff speed, generating enough lift to overcome nearly 400 tons of weight. Commercial jets typically climb at around 10-15 degrees during initial ascent.

components.note: 又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 两国政府一直保持友好关系。
example.pinyin: liǎng guó zhèngfǔ yìzhí bǎochí yǒuhǎo guānxì.
example.english: The two governments have always maintained friendly relations.
example.fact: China has practiced "panda diplomacy" since the 1950s, most famously sending pandas Ling-Ling and Hsing-Hsing to the US National Zoo in 1972 after Nixon's visit. Pandas are still loaned rather than gifted today, under agreements requiring cubs born abroad to eventually return to China. This practice reflects how animals have long served as tools of international goodwill.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plant) — the raw material, wood or grass cut for fuel.
新 (new, freshly cut) sits above it — freshly-cut fuel wood, giving 薪 its meaning 'firewood,' later extended to 'salary.'
水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.

example.hanzi: 他每个月的薪水都存起来了。
example.pinyin: tā měi gè yuè de xīnshuǐ dōu cún qǐlái le.
example.english: He saves his salary every month.
example.fact: The English word "salary" comes from the Latin "salarium," believed to relate to salt (sal), since Roman soldiers were sometimes paid partly in salt, a valuable commodity in the ancient world. Salt was so prized that it was used as currency across many ancient civilizations, from Rome to West Africa. This history is why we still say someone is "worth their salt."

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哈 is the sound made by the mouth while laughing
合 (hé) gives a sound related to 哈's reading hā, from an older, closer pronunciation link
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.

example.hanzi: 我的朋友哈里来自澳大利亚。
example.pinyin: wǒ de péngyou Hālǐ láizì Àodàlìyà.
example.english: My friend Harry is from Australia.
example.fact: Harry Houdini, born Erik Weisz in Budapest in 1874, became the most famous escape artist in history, freeing himself from locked chains, straitjackets, and sealed containers underwater. He died in 1926 from a ruptured appendix, reportedly after being punched in the stomach by a skeptic testing his claims. Houdini spent his later years actively debunking fraudulent spiritualists.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 反 pictures pushing against a steep surface.
又 (a hand) — a hand pushing back against a cliff gave 反 its meaning 'to turn over' or 'opposite.'

example.hanzi: 他的意见和我的正好相反。
example.pinyin: tā de yìjiàn hé wǒ de zhènghǎo xiāngfǎn.
example.english: His opinion is exactly the opposite of mine.
example.fact: In physics, matter and antimatter are near-perfect opposites: every particle has an antiparticle with the same mass but opposite charge, and when they meet they annihilate each other, converting their mass entirely into energy. The universe appears to be made almost entirely of matter, and physicists still don't fully understand why matter overwhelmingly won out over antimatter after the Big Bang. This asymmetry remains one of the biggest open questions in particle physics.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 没 originally meant to sink or drown in water, later extended to the negative 'not have.'
殳 (shū) is the historical sound component; it no longer rhymes with méi in modern Mandarin, another case of sound drift over time.
用's oracle-bone form is thought to depict either a wooden bucket or a tortoise-shell prepared for divination; the character was later used to mean 'to use, to employ.'

example.hanzi: 这把旧伞已经没用了。
example.pinyin: zhè bǎ jiù sǎn yǐjīng méiyòng le.
example.english: This old umbrella is useless now.
example.fact: The appendix was long considered a useless evolutionary leftover, but research now suggests it may serve as a reservoir for beneficial gut bacteria, helping to repopulate the intestines after illnesses like severe diarrhea. Charles Darwin himself speculated about the appendix's function in the 19th century. Other "vestigial" structures, like the wisdom teeth and tailbone, are being reexamined by modern biologists too.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 波 refers to waves on water
皮 (pí) gives a sound close to 波's reading bō, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
士 is thought to depict either a battle-axe or a craftsman's tool; the character came to signify a capable man, and later a scholar-official or 'gentleman.'
页 (head) — 顿 originally related to bowing the head, i.e. a pause or stop
屯 (tún) gives a sound distantly related to 顿's reading dùn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 波士顿是美国历史最悠久的城市之一。
example.pinyin: Bōshìdùn shì Měiguó lìshǐ zuì yōujiǔ de chéngshì zhī yī.
example.english: Boston is one of the oldest cities in the United States.
example.fact: Boston was founded in 1630 by Puritan settlers and is home to the Boston Tea Party site, where colonists dumped 342 chests of British tea into the harbor in 1773 to protest taxation. The city also hosts the Boston Marathon, first run in 1897, making it the world's oldest annually contested marathon. Boston's subway, opened in 1897, was the first underground rapid transit system in the Americas.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — 资 relates to wealth, funds, and resources.
次 (cì) gives a hint of the sound — 资 is pronounced zī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.

example.hanzi: 公司急需资金来扩大生产。
example.pinyin: gōngsī jíxū zījīn lái kuòdà shēngchǎn.
example.english: The company urgently needs funds to expand production.
example.fact: Venture capital as an industry traces back to 1946, when Georges Doriot, a Harvard Business School professor, founded American Research and Development Corporation, one of the first firms to systematically fund small companies with high growth potential. His $70,000 investment in Digital Equipment Corporation in 1957 grew to be worth over $355 million by 1971. This model of pooling capital to fund risky new ventures became the template for modern Silicon Valley investing.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 室 refers to an enclosed room under a roof
至 (zhì) gives the sound — an exact match with 室's reading shì
又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'

example.hanzi: 我和室友一起打扫了宿舍。
example.pinyin: wǒ hé shìyǒu yìqǐ dǎsǎo le sùshè.
example.english: My roommate and I cleaned the dorm room together.
example.fact: Albert Einstein and Marcel Grossmann were classmates and close friends at the Swiss Federal Polytechnic in Zurich; Grossmann later provided the mathematical framework of differential geometry that Einstein needed to formulate general relativity. Their long friendship shows how student relationships can echo for decades. Grossmann's notes from their shared coursework were reportedly essential to Einstein passing his exams.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 做 relates to a person carrying out an action.
故 (cause, reason, to happen) — combined with 亻 (person), 做 came to mean 'to make' or 'to do,' someone actively causing something to happen.
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 她把每件事情都做好了。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ měi jiàn shìqing dōu zuòhǎo le.
example.english: She did everything well.
example.fact: The Toyota Production System, developed in Japan after World War II, popularized "kaizen," or continuous improvement, where workers on the line are empowered to stop production the moment they spot a defect. This philosophy of doing things right the first time helped transform Toyota from a small loom-making company into one of the world's largest automakers by the 1980s. Many modern quality-control systems in manufacturing trace directly back to these post-war Japanese practices.

components.note: 日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.
日 (sun) — the sun is what disappears as evening falls
免 (to escape, avoid) — pictured as the sun slipping away, giving 晚 its sense of 'late, evening'

example.hanzi: 明晚我们一起去看电影吧。
example.pinyin: míngwǎn wǒmen yìqǐ qù kàn diànyǐng ba.
example.english: Let's go watch a movie together tomorrow evening.
example.fact: Early cinemas in the late 1890s often struggled because projector bulbs were too weak to compete with daylight, so theaters actively sought darkened rooms and evening showtimes to make the image visible. This is part of why "going to the movies" became associated with nighttime outings. Modern digital projectors are now bright enough to run matinee showings without any issue.

components.note: 厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 原 relates to a source high up, such as a spring emerging from rock.
泉 (quán) gives a hint of the sound — 原 is pronounced yuán, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
贝 (a shell, an ancient form of currency/valuables) — represents the property or standards that rules protect.
刂 (a knife) — depicts laws being carved or inscribed onto a slate, the source of 则's meaning 'rule, standard.'

example.hanzi: 诚实是他做人的原则。
example.pinyin: chéngshí shì tā zuòrén de yuánzé.
example.english: Honesty is his principle in life.
example.fact: The Hippocratic Oath, traditionally attributed to the ancient Greek physician Hippocrates around the 5th century BC, established one of the earliest recorded sets of ethical principles for a profession, including a commitment to "do no harm." Modern versions are still recited by many medical school graduates today, though the wording has been revised repeatedly over the centuries. The original oath also included a pledge never to give a lethal drug, even if asked.

components.note: 王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.
知 (to know) forms the upper part of the character.
日 (sun, clarity) — knowledge seen as clearly as the sun gave 智 its meaning 'wisdom.'

example.hanzi: 遇到麻烦时，他总是很理智。
example.pinyin: yùdào máfan shí, tā zǒngshì hěn lǐzhì.
example.english: When facing trouble, he is always very rational.
example.fact: The prefrontal cortex, the brain region most associated with rational decision-making and impulse control, is one of the last parts of the human brain to fully mature, typically not finishing development until the mid-twenties. This is part of why neuroscientists caution against treating teenage brains as simply smaller adult brains. The famous 19th-century case of Phineas Gage, who survived a railroad spike through his frontal lobe, was one of the first pieces of evidence linking this brain region to personality and judgment.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — used when asking a question aloud
那 (nà) gives a sound close to 哪's reading nǎ, differing mainly in tone
忄 (heart) — 怕 relates to a feeling of fear in one's heart
白 (bái) gives a loose sound connection to 怕's reading pà

example.hanzi: 哪怕下雨，我们也要出发。
example.pinyin: nǎpà xiàyǔ, wǒmen yě yào chūfā.
example.english: Even if it rains, we still have to set off.
example.fact: Ernest Shackleton's 1914 Antarctic expedition became stranded when their ship Endurance was crushed by pack ice, yet he led all 28 crew members to safety through an 800-mile open-boat journey across the Southern Ocean to reach help. Even facing near-certain death, the crew survived without a single loss of life. The wreck of the Endurance itself was finally located on the seafloor in 2022, more than a century later.

components.note: 圭, made of two 土 (earth) stacked together, depicts a handful of mortar or soil.
寸 (a hand/small measure) — sealing something shut with packed mortar gave 封 its meaning 'to seal, to close.'
钅 (metal) shows 锁 is typically a metal object.
⺌ (a form of 小) gives a sound distantly related to suǒ, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 敌军对港口实施了封锁。
example.pinyin: díjūn duì gǎngkǒu shíshī le fēngsuǒ.
example.english: The enemy forces imposed a blockade on the port.
example.fact: The Berlin Blockade of 1948-49 saw the Soviet Union cut off all ground access to West Berlin, prompting the Western Allies to respond with the Berlin Airlift, flying in food, fuel, and supplies around the clock for nearly 11 months. At its peak, planes were landing roughly every 45 seconds. The blockade ultimately failed, and the Soviets lifted it in May 1949, marking an early Cold War victory for the West.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — represents words being spoken.
斥 (to reprimand, blame) — words of accusation or complaint gave 诉 its meaning 'to sue, to tell, to complain.'
Speech — litigation involves speaking/arguing a case.
Gives the sound gōng, related to sòng but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这场诉讼持续了整整三年。
example.pinyin: zhè chǎng sùsòng chíxù le zhěngzhěng sān nián.
example.english: This lawsuit lasted a full three years.
example.fact: Some real-world court cases have dragged on for decades, inspiring Charles Dickens's novel "Bleak House," which satirized England's slow-moving Chancery Court through the fictional case Jarndyce and Jarndyce. Prolonged litigation of this kind has historically been cited as evidence in pushes for judicial reform. Modern court systems in many countries now track case-processing times specifically to identify and prevent such extreme delays.

components.note: 高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.

example.hanzi: 这座山的高度超过五千米。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò shān de gāodù chāoguò wǔqiān mǐ.
example.english: This mountain's height exceeds five thousand meters.
example.fact: Mount Everest, the world's tallest mountain above sea level at 8,849 meters, is actually still growing by a few millimeters each year due to the ongoing collision between the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates. Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller when measured from its base on the ocean floor, at over 10,000 meters total. Everest's summit height has been re-measured multiple times using GPS and satellite technology, most recently confirmed by a joint China-Nepal survey in 2020.

meanings: variant of 記錄|记录[ji4 lu4]

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 纪 relates to organizing threads in order, extended to mean 'record, era'
己 (jǐ) gives a sound close to 纪's reading jì
录 traditionally depicted a hand-held tool used for carving or writing records — the image behind its meaning 'to record, to write down.'

example.hanzi: 他打破了世界纪录。
example.pinyin: tā dǎpò le shìjiè jìlù.
example.english: He broke the world record.
example.fact: Usain Bolt's 100-meter world record of 9.58 seconds, set at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin, has stood longer than any other man's 100m record in the sport's modern era. Scientists have calculated that Bolt reached a peak speed of over 44 km/h during that race. His stride length, at nearly 2.7 meters per step, is unusually long for a sprinter of his height.

components.note: 王 here is not 'king' but a simplified string of three jade discs threaded on a cord.
丶 is the extra dot added to distinguish 玉 (jade) from 王 (king), representing the gem itself.
米 depicts scattered grains of husked rice around a central stalk — a simple picture giving 米 its meaning 'rice, grain.'

example.hanzi: 农民正在地里收玉米。
example.pinyin: nóngmín zhèngzài dì lǐ shōu yùmǐ.
example.english: The farmers are harvesting corn in the field.
example.fact: Corn was domesticated from a wild grass called teosinte in southern Mexico roughly 9,000 years ago, and its ears were originally only a few centimeters long with just a handful of kernels. Selective breeding by Indigenous farmers over thousands of years transformed it into the large-eared crop grown today. Corn is now the most widely produced grain crop in the world by volume, exceeding both wheat and rice.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
囗 (an enclosure) surrounds the character.
大 (a person with arms outstretched) sits inside the enclosure — a picture of someone relying on their surroundings, giving 因 its senses 'to rely on' and, by extension, 'cause, reason.'

example.hanzi: 这种疾病和基因有关。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng jíbìng hé jīyīn yǒuguān.
example.english: This disease is related to genes.
example.fact: The Human Genome Project, completed in 2003, mapped roughly 3 billion base pairs of human DNA at a cost of about $2.7 billion and took 13 years. Today, sequencing an entire human genome can be done in a single day for a few hundred dollars. Humans share about 60% of their genes with bananas and roughly 98.8% with chimpanzees.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
司 depicts a person with a raised arm giving orders — an official directing others, giving rise to the meaning 'to manage' or 'to take charge of.'

example.hanzi: 我的上司要求我们下周完成报告。
example.pinyin: wǒ de shàngsi yāoqiú wǒmen xià zhōu wánchéng bàogào.
example.english: My boss requires us to finish the report next week.
example.fact: The English word "boss" derives from the Dutch "baas," meaning master, brought to America by Dutch settlers in New York (originally New Amsterdam) in the 17th century. It caught on partly because "master" carried uncomfortable associations with slavery in the American context. This borrowing is one of many Dutch-origin words, like "cookie" and "coleslaw," still used in American English today.

components.note: 宀 (roof/shelter) — 宠 relates to being kept and favored within a household.
龙 (lóng) gives a sound only distantly related to chǒng today, having drifted apart over time.
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 她养了一只可爱的宠物狗。
example.pinyin: tā yǎng le yì zhī kě'ài de chǒngwù gǒu.
example.english: She has an adorable pet dog.
example.fact: Dogs were likely the first animals domesticated by humans, with genetic evidence suggesting the split between wolves and dogs occurred somewhere between 20,000 and 40,000 years ago. Ancient burial sites, such as one in Germany dating back roughly 14,000 years, have been found containing dogs buried alongside their human companions, suggesting an emotional bond even then. Today, dogs are kept as pets in an estimated one in three households worldwide.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun is what disappears as evening falls
免 (to escape, avoid) — pictured as the sun slipping away, giving 晚 its sense of 'late, evening'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 学校为新生举办了一场晚会。
example.pinyin: xuéxiào wèi xīnshēng jǔbàn le yì chǎng wǎnhuì.
example.english: The school held an evening party for new students.
example.fact: New Year's Eve celebrations trace back to ancient Babylon around 2000 BC, where the new year was marked near the spring equinox with an 11-day festival called Akitu. The tradition of using January 1st specifically dates to the Roman calendar reform under Julius Caesar in 46 BC, who named the month after Janus, the two-faced god of beginnings. Fireworks, now a global staple of such evening celebrations, originated in China over a thousand years ago as a byproduct of gunpowder experimentation.

components.note: 广 depicts a lean-to shelter built against a wall or cliff, open on one side — the image behind its meaning 'wide, spacious' and its use as the 'building' radical.
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 每天早上都有人在广场上跳舞。
example.pinyin: měitiān zǎoshang dōu yǒu rén zài guǎngchǎng shàng tiàowǔ.
example.english: Every morning there are people dancing in the square.
example.fact: St. Peter's Square in Vatican City was designed by the sculptor and architect Gian Lorenzo Bernini in the 17th century, with its elliptical colonnade of 284 columns arranged to symbolically embrace visitors like outstretched arms. The square can hold around 300,000 people during major papal events. Its central obelisk was originally brought from Egypt by the Roman Emperor Caligula in 37 AD.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — an old link between listening to official duties and 职's meaning 'duty, profession, office'
只 (zhī) gives a loose sound connection to 职's reading zhí
亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.

example.hanzi: 他终于得到了梦想的职位。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú dédào le mèngxiǎng de zhíwèi.
example.english: He finally got his dream position.
example.fact: China's imperial examination system, established during the Sui Dynasty around 605 AD, tested candidates for government positions and lasted for roughly 1,300 years until it was abolished in 1905. Candidates could spend decades preparing and retaking the exams, and passing could elevate a commoner into the ruling class. This meritocratic model later influenced the design of civil service systems in Britain and the United States in the 19th century.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 称 originally referred to weighing grain on a scale, extending to 'to weigh' and, later, 'to call, to name.'
尔 is a simplified stand-in for the historical phonetic component 爯; it is close in sound to chēng in an older reading, though the two have drifted apart since.
为's traditional form 為 depicted a hand grasping the trunk of an elephant, symbolizing training an elephant to work — the source of 为's meaning 'to do, to act,' and by extension 'for, because of.'

example.hanzi: 这种植物被称为“沙漠之王”。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng zhíwù bèi chēngwéi “shāmò zhī wáng”.
example.english: This plant is called the "king of the desert."
example.fact: Welwitschia mirabilis, a strange desert plant native to Namibia and Angola, is sometimes called a "living fossil" because individual plants can live for well over 1,000 years, with some estimated at nearly 2,000 years old. It survives in one of the driest deserts on Earth by absorbing moisture from coastal fog through its leaves. Despite its resilience, it produces only two leaves in its entire lifetime, which simply keep growing and splitting.

components.note: 黄 originally depicted a large ornamental jade pendant worn at the waist; the character was later borrowed for the color 'yellow.'
⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'

example.hanzi: 秋天的时候，很多叶子都变成了黄色。
example.pinyin: qiūtiān de shíhou, hěn duō yèzi dōu biànchéng le huángsè.
example.english: In autumn, many leaves turn yellow.
example.fact: Autumn leaves turn yellow because chlorophyll, the green pigment used for photosynthesis, breaks down as days shorten and temperatures drop, revealing yellow and orange carotenoid pigments that were present in the leaf all along but masked by the dominant green. These carotenoids are the same class of pigments that give carrots their color. Red pigments, by contrast, are often newly produced in autumn rather than simply unmasked.

components.note: 丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
心 (heart) — 恶 relates to an evil or malicious state of heart/mind
亚 (yà) gives a sound distantly related to 恶's reading è, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 这种欺骗行为真是可恶。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng qīpiàn xíngwéi zhēnshi kěwù.
example.english: This kind of deceptive behavior is truly repulsive.
example.fact: The blobfish, often voted the world's "ugliest animal," only looks gelatinous and repulsive when removed from the deep-sea pressure it normally lives under, at depths of 600 to 1,200 meters off the coast of Australia. In its natural habitat, the pressure keeps its body properly shaped, and it actually looks like an ordinary fish. It won the title of world's ugliest animal in a 2013 poll by the Ugly Animal Preservation Society, intended to raise awareness for unglamorous endangered species.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng

example.hanzi: 今晚的星星特别明亮。
example.pinyin: jīnwǎn de xīngxing tèbié míngliàng.
example.english: Tonight's stars are especially bright.
example.fact: The light from most stars visible to the naked eye left those stars years, centuries, or even millennia ago, meaning we are essentially looking into the past every time we look up at the night sky. The nearest star system to our sun, Alpha Centauri, is about 4.37 light-years away, so its light takes over four years to reach Earth. Some stars we see may have already died by the time their light finally arrives.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
一 (one) — relates to 百's meaning 'hundred,' a large round number built from 'one.'
白 (bái) gives a sound hint — 百 is pronounced bǎi, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这本书一共有一百页。
example.pinyin: zhè běn shū yígòng yǒu yìbǎi yè.
example.english: This book has one hundred pages in total.
example.fact: The abacus, one of the earliest calculating tools, was used in ancient China, Rome, and Mesopotamia to perform arithmetic including counting in the hundreds, long before written positional number systems became widespread. Skilled abacus users in East Asia can still outperform calculators for certain addition and subtraction tasks through a technique called "anzan," mental abacus calculation. Some Japanese schools continue to teach abacus use specifically to strengthen mental math ability.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 确 originally meant firm and solid like stone, extending to 'true, accurate, indeed.'
角 (jiǎo) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from què.
刀 (knife) — relates directly to 切's meaning 'to cut.'
七 (qī) gives a sound hint — 切 is pronounced qiè, sharing the same initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 他没有给出确切的答案。
example.pinyin: tā méiyǒu gěi chū quèqiè de dá'àn.
example.english: He didn't give a definite answer.
example.fact: The value of pi has been calculated to over 100 trillion digits using modern supercomputers, even though only about 40 digits are needed for any practical engineering calculation, including plotting a spacecraft's trajectory to the edge of the observable universe with atomic-level precision. Ancient Babylonian mathematicians approximated pi as 3.125 nearly 4,000 years ago. The pursuit of ever more exact digits today is mostly a way to stress-test computing hardware.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching out for support.
十 (a branch) — held in the hand, the image of support giving 支 its meaning 'to support, prop up; branch.'
扌 (hand) — 援 describes reaching out to help someone by hand.
爰 depicts one hand passing something to another, reinforcing the idea of lending aid — together giving 援 its meaning 'to help, to aid.'

example.hanzi: 各地纷纷派出医疗队支援灾区。
example.pinyin: gèdì fēnfēn pàichū yīliáoduì zhīyuán zāiqū.
example.english: Regions everywhere sent medical teams to support the disaster area.
example.fact: The Marshall Plan, launched by the United States in 1948, provided about $13 billion (equivalent to well over $150 billion today) in economic support to help rebuild sixteen war-torn Western European countries after World War II. The aid helped rebuild infrastructure, stabilize currencies, and is widely credited with helping prevent the spread of communism in Western Europe during the early Cold War. Secretary of State George Marshall received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1953 for the initiative.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — 限 relates to a boundary or limit on a place
艮 (gèn) gives a loose sound connection to 限's reading xiàn
刂 (knife) — 制 relates to cutting and shaping, and by extension, to making or controlling something.
巾 (jīn) gives a hint of the sound — 制 is pronounced zhì, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 医生限制他每天摄入的糖分。
example.pinyin: yīshēng xiànzhì tā měitiān shèrù de tángfèn.
example.english: The doctor restricts his daily sugar intake.
example.fact: The world's first speed limit, imposed by the UK's Locomotive Act of 1865, capped "horseless carriages" at 4 mph in the country and required a person to walk ahead waving a red flag to warn pedestrians. This "Red Flag Act" was eventually repealed in 1896 as automobiles became more common and drivers pushed back against the restriction. The modern concept of speed limits tied to road design and safety data only emerged in the 20th century.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — represents an action performed by hand.
戈 (a spear/dagger-axe) — an old image of searching or probing with a weapon in hand, giving 找 its meaning 'to search, to look for.'
回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'

example.hanzi: 她终于找回了丢失的钱包。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú zhǎohuí le diūshī de qiánbāo.
example.english: She finally retrieved her lost wallet.
example.fact: The Antikythera mechanism, recovered from a Greek shipwreck in 1901, is a hand-cranked bronze device built around 150-100 BC that could predict eclipses and track the positions of the sun, moon, and planets — historians consider it the world's oldest known analog computer. It sat corroded on the seafloor for roughly 2,000 years before sponge divers found it. Researchers are still using X-ray imaging today to decode inscriptions on its fragments.

components.note: A stylized foot (related to 止, 'to stop/foot') — originally meant 'to go,' later grammaticalized into a literary possessive/linking particle, similar to 的.
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 在他的领导之下，公司业绩大幅提升。
example.pinyin: zài tā de lǐngdǎo zhīxià, gōngsī yèjì dàfú tíshēng.
example.english: Under his leadership, the company's performance improved significantly.
example.fact: Roughly 71% of Earth's surface lies under the ocean, yet more than 80% of that underwater world remains unmapped and unexplored in any real detail, according to NOAA. We actually have more detailed maps of the surface of Mars and the Moon than we do of our own ocean floor. The deepest known point, the Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep, plunges nearly 11,000 meters below sea level.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, body) — 肮 (as in 肮脏, dirty) describes something unclean, grouped under the body/flesh radical here.
亢 (kàng) gives a sound distantly related to āng, sharing the same final but having drifted apart in initial consonant over time.
⺼ (flesh) shows 脏 (zàng) relates to the body, as in internal organs.
庄 (zhuāng) gives a sound close to zàng, sharing a similar consonant sound though the vowel and ending differ.

example.hanzi: 街道两旁堆满了肮脏的垃圾。
example.pinyin: jiēdào liǎngpáng duī mǎn le āngzāng de lājī.
example.english: Piles of filthy garbage lined both sides of the street.
example.fact: London's Great Stink of 1858 was so severe — caused by raw sewage flowing directly into the Thames during a summer heatwave — that it reportedly drove Parliament to finally fund a massive new sewer system, designed by engineer Joseph Bazalgette. That system, completed in the 1870s, dramatically reduced outbreaks of cholera in the city and is still partly in use today. Before this, doctors mistakenly believed diseases like cholera spread through foul-smelling air rather than contaminated water.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.
一 (a hairpin) — worn across the top of the head to mark a coming-of-age ceremony, giving 夫 its meaning 'man, husband.'

example.hanzi: 这位大夫在朝廷任职多年。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi dàfū zài cháotíng rènzhí duō nián.
example.english: This senior official has served in the imperial court for many years.
example.fact: In ancient China's Zhou dynasty aristocratic hierarchy, "dàfū" denoted a rank of nobility below feudal lords but above common officials, roughly comparable to a minister or senior court official. Over time, the same characters came to colloquially mean "physician" in modern Mandarin, pronounced with a different tone, reflecting how court physicians once held elevated status. This dual meaning still causes confusion for language learners today.

components.note: 无 (a simplified form of 無) originally depicted a person holding ornamented sleeves or plumes while dancing; the character was borrowed for its sound to mean 'nothing, without,' and the dance meaning was later given its own character, 舞.
攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 数 relates to the action of counting.
娄 (lóu) gives a hint of the sound — 数 is pronounced shù, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 天空中有无数颗星星。
example.pinyin: tiānkōng zhōng yǒu wúshù kē xīngxing.
example.english: There are countless stars in the sky.
example.fact: Astronomers estimate there are more stars in the observable universe than grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches — roughly 10^24 stars compared to an estimated 10^18 to 10^20 grains of sand. Yet on a clear night without light pollution, the human eye can typically see only about 2,500 to 5,000 individual stars at once. The Milky Way alone is thought to contain 100 to 400 billion stars.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 排 relates to arranging things by hand into order
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to 排's reading pái, having drifted apart over time
纟 (thread) — 练 originally meant to boil and whiten silk thread, extending to 'to practice, to train' through repeated refinement.
柬 (jiǎn) gives a sound distantly related to liàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 演员们正在为演出排练。
example.pinyin: yǎnyuánmen zhèngzài wèi yǎnchū páiliàn.
example.english: The actors are rehearsing for the performance.
example.fact: The Metropolitan Opera in New York typically rehearses a new production for six to eight weeks before opening night, with singers, orchestra, and stagehands coordinating hundreds of technical cues. Maria Callas, one of the most famous opera singers of the 20th century, was known for insisting on exhaustive rehearsals to perfect both her vocal technique and dramatic acting. Even after decades of experience, professional performers rarely skip rehearsal for a new role.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 评 relates to speaking judgments or opinions about something
平 (píng) gives the sound — an exact match with 评's reading píng
讠 (speech) — 论 relates to discussing or explaining something with words.
仑 (logical order, arrangement) — combined with speech, 论 came to mean 'to discuss' or 'a theory,' explaining ideas in an orderly way.

example.hanzi: 这篇文章引起了很多评论。
example.pinyin: zhè piān wénzhāng yǐnqǐ le hěn duō pínglùn.
example.english: This article sparked a lot of commentary.
example.fact: The world's first newspaper opinion columns are often traced to 18th-century London publications like The Spectator, founded in 1711 by Joseph Addison and Richard Steele, which used a fictional narrator to comment on daily life and social manners. It ran for only about two years but influenced essay writing and journalism for generations after. Its format — short, witty daily commentary — is considered a direct ancestor of the modern opinion column.

meanings: (idiom) to stand out from the crowd

components.note: 与's ancient form pictured two hands jointly lifting or offering an object — an image of giving or participating together, which gave 与 its meanings 'and, with, to give.'
人 (person), tripled — three people together depict a crowd, giving 众 its meaning 'many, multitude.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'

example.hanzi: 她的穿衣风格总是与众不同。
example.pinyin: tā de chuānyī fēnggé zǒngshì yǔzhòngbùtóng.
example.english: Her style of dress always stands out from the crowd.
example.fact: The axolotl, a salamander native to Mexico's Xochimilco wetlands, stands out among amphibians because it typically never undergoes full metamorphosis, retaining its gills and aquatic juvenile form throughout its adult life, a trait called neoteny. It's also famous for its extraordinary ability to fully regenerate lost limbs, its spinal cord, and even parts of its heart and brain without scarring. Scientists study axolotls closely, hoping to unlock clues for regenerative medicine in humans.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — food offered generously to another person
口 (mouth) — kind words spoken alongside the gift

良's oracle-bone form is thought to depict a section of a granary or corridor open at both ends, allowing grain to be cleaned as it passed through — a picture of refinement extended to mean 'good, fine.'

example.hanzi: 她心地善良，总是帮助别人。
example.pinyin: tā xīndì shànliáng, zǒngshì bāngzhù biérén.
example.english: She is kindhearted and always helps others.
example.fact: Studies in behavioral science have found that acts of kindness activate the brain's reward circuitry in ways similar to receiving a reward oneself, a phenomenon sometimes called the "helper's high." Research by social psychologists has also shown that witnessing someone else's generosity can inspire onlookers to behave more kindly themselves, an effect known as moral elevation. Some researchers argue this cascading effect helps explain how cooperative behavior spreads through communities.

components.note: 丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
心 (heart) — 悲 relates to a heavy, sorrowful heart.
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to bēi, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他的处境实在可悲。
example.pinyin: tā de chǔjìng shízài kěbēi.
example.english: His situation is truly lamentable.
example.fact: The dodo, a flightless bird native only to the island of Mauritius, went extinct within roughly a century of European sailors arriving in the late 16th century, done in by hunting, introduced predators, and habitat destruction. It became one of the most cited symbols of human-caused extinction, giving rise to the phrase "dead as a dodo." No complete skeleton of a dodo survives today; scientific reconstructions rely on scattered bones and a handful of contemporary illustrations.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
冫 (water) — 准 originally referred to a carpenter's level using water to check flatness, extended to 'standard, accurate, level.'
隹 (zhuī) gives a sound hint — 准 is pronounced zhǔn, sharing the base sound though the vowel and tone differ somewhat.

example.hanzi: 图书馆里不准大声说话。
example.pinyin: túshūguǎn lǐ bùzhǔn dàshēng shuōhuà.
example.english: Loud talking is not allowed in the library.
example.fact: Venice has banned large cruise ships from its historic lagoon since 2021, after years of concern that the massive vessels were eroding the foundations of the centuries-old city and disturbing its fragile ecosystem. The city had already been listed by UNESCO as at risk partly due to the strain from mass tourism. Cruise passengers must now dock at a more distant industrial port and transfer into the city by other means.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.

example.hanzi: 这家公司管理着一个大型投资基金。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī guǎnlǐzhe yí gè dàxíng tóuzī jījīn.
example.english: This company manages a large investment fund.
example.fact: The Norwegian Government Pension Fund Global, often called simply "the Oil Fund," is one of the largest sovereign wealth funds in the world, holding over $1.4 trillion in assets built from the country's oil and gas revenue since 1996. It owns small stakes in thousands of companies across nearly every country on Earth, and by some estimates owns roughly 1.5% of all publicly listed companies worldwide. The fund is managed under strict ethical investment guidelines that have led it to divest from companies involved in coal, tobacco, and certain weapons manufacturing.

components.note: 王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'

example.hanzi: 这支球队赢得了全国冠军。
example.pinyin: zhè zhī qiúduì yíngdé le quánguó guànjūn.
example.english: This team won the national championship.
example.fact: The English football club Sheffield FC, founded in 1857, is recognized by FIFA as the oldest association football club in the world still in existence today. It predates the founding of the English Football Association itself by six years, and some of its early rules directly influenced the sport's modern laws. The club still plays in England's lower non-league divisions.

components.note: 又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'
讠 (speech) — 谊 relates to words exchanged between friends.
宜 (fitting, suitable) sits beside it — speech that is fitting and warm, giving 谊 its meaning 'friendship.'

example.hanzi: 他们之间的友谊持续了三十年。
example.pinyin: tāmen zhījiān de yǒuyì chíxù le sānshí nián.
example.english: Their friendship has lasted thirty years.
example.fact: Harvard's Study of Adult Development, which has tracked participants for over 80 years since 1938, found that the quality of a person's close relationships, including friendships, is one of the strongest predictors of happiness and even physical health in old age — a stronger predictor than wealth, fame, or IQ. The study is one of the longest-running research projects on human life ever conducted. Its lead researchers have continued publishing findings well into the 21st century.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.

example.hanzi: 下雨了，我们还是别出门了。
example.pinyin: xiàyǔ le, wǒmen háishì bié chūmén le.
example.english: It's raining, let's not go out.
example.fact: The invention of the umbrella dates back over 3,000 years, with early depictions found in ancient Egyptian, Assyrian, and Chinese art, though these early versions were primarily used as sunshades for royalty rather than rain protection. Waterproofing umbrellas for rain became common much later, and the folding umbrella wasn't widely popularized in the West until the 18th century. Jonas Hanway, an English philanthropist, is often credited with popularizing rain umbrellas for men in London around 1750, despite public ridicule at the time.

components.note: 十 — traditionally read as a great man standing tall.
一 (the two horizontal strokes) — heaven above and earth below, which the king bridges, giving 王 its meaning 'king, monarch.'
Two lines curving apart from each other, originally meaning 'to divide, split' — the shape was later adopted to represent the number 'eight.'

example.hanzi: 河里游着一只王八。
example.pinyin: hé lǐ yóuzhe yì zhī wángba.
example.english: A softshell turtle is swimming in the river.
example.fact: The Chinese softshell turtle can absorb oxygen directly through specialized skin structures in its throat and cloaca, allowing it to stay submerged in water for extended periods without surfacing to breathe air. This adaptation, called cloacal respiration, is also seen in some other freshwater turtle species. Softshell turtles are farmed extensively in parts of East Asia both for food and traditional medicine markets.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 全国代表大会将在北京召开。
example.pinyin: quánguó dàibiǎo dàhuì jiāng zài Běijīng zhàokāi.
example.english: The National People's Congress will convene in Beijing.
example.fact: The United Nations General Assembly, first convened in London in January 1946, now brings together representatives from 193 member states annually in New York to debate global issues ranging from climate change to international security. Its General Debate each September regularly causes the biggest security and traffic disruption of the year in Manhattan. Each member state, regardless of size or population, gets exactly one vote in the Assembly.
